name: Cyclops, Tartalo
body:
Cyclops, Tartalo
CR 5

This brutish humanoid stands nearly three times the height of a human, with a single eye glaring out beneath a beetling brow. It is dressed in rough sheepskins, but a gleaming gold ring adorns one of its fingers.

XP 1,600
NE Large humanoid (giant)
Init -1; Senses low-light vision, scent; Perception +1

DEFENSE

AC 15, touch 8, flat-footed 15 (-1 Dex, +7 natural, –1 size)
hp 59 (7d8+28)
Fort +9, Ref +1, Will +3
Defensive Abilities ferocity, rock catching; DR 5/piercing

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee spear +10 (2d6+7) or 2 slams +9 (1d8 +5)
Ranged spear +4 (2d6+5) or rock +5 (2d8+7)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks rock throwing (120 ft.)

STATISTICS

Str 21 Dex 8, Con 19, Int 6, Wis 13, Cha 12
Base Atk +5; CMB +11; CMD 18
Feats Cornugon Smash, Intimidating Prowess, Power Attack, Weapon Focus (spear)
Skills Craft (jewelry) +10, Intimidate +14, Profession (shepherd) +5; Racial Modifiers +8 Craft (jewelry)
Languages Common, Giant
SQ cursed ring, poor depth perception

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Poor Depth Perception

Tartalo cyclops have difficulty with their depth perception suffering –4 to sight based perception checks and –4 on ranged attacks beyond 30 ft.

Cursed Ring (Su)

Tartalo cyclops forge a ring that they imbue with a captured spirit. Once per day, the tartalo cyclops can ask the ring for magical aid as a swift action to immediately cast aid, blood armor, or cure moderate wounds (CL 7). This does not provoke attacks of opportunity.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate or warm hills or mountains
Organization solitary, pair, or gang (3-5)
Treasure standard (large spear, cursed ring, other treasure)

These one-eyed giants dwell in temperate and subtropical hilly and mountainous regions. Tartalos are generally solitary, living alone in large, spacious caves. Occasionally, mated pairs or small family groups with children are encountered.

Tartalos raise herd animals such as sheep or goats, grazing them on the slopes near their home, and bringing their herd into their cave home with them at night.

While tartalos mainly subsist on the flesh of their herd animals, they crave the taste of humanoid flesh. If a lone hunter, lost hikers, or band of wayward travelers pass near their lair, a tartalo is sure to attack if it notices them, eager for a meal.
